_doc: The drawn look (client only; read by src/client/look.ts). style: real (the park painted with the 26 photos, sky light, sun, physically based materials; see real._doc), cute (toon light, ink outlines, painted park) or grey (the flat greybox with edge lines, for judging shape). paint picks a colour per park element: by element id, then role, then feature type, then collection; buildings cycle through buildings[]. toon.bands: light levels from shadow to full sun. outline: ink colour, width in px, crease = how sharp a fold must be to get a line, fade = metres where lines fade out. sun.from: where the sun sits relative to the skater (m).

real._doc: The real look. sky.hdri: an overcast sky (assets/real, CC0 Poly Haven) that lights the park (environment) and shows behind it (background); turn rotates it (degrees); highlights: sky luminance above knee is softly compressed (to at most knee + span) so the bright overcast dome keeps its clouds. exposure: filmic tone-mapping exposure. sun: direction is fixed in the world (m, relative to the park), shadowMap = texels across the whole park. atlasGain scales the photo paint (the photos already hold the day's light). unseen: where no photo saw a surface, the tiling detail shows albedo times harder, plus stains (strength) from the same texture at stainScale metres per tile. nearFade: walls and columns (not ground) closer to the camera than these metres dissolve (fully gone at the first), so a column beside the lens never fills the frame. ao: ambient occlusion radius (m), strength, resolution (fraction of the screen), samples and denoise taps (AO is the frame's biggest cost; at 0.4 with 12/8 it looks the same as 0.5 with 16/16 and costs about 2 ms less at 3200x1800). detail: tiling surface textures by kind, scale = metres per tile, albedo/normal/rough = how strongly each shows. materials: park material (from the skatepark palette) to detail kind. pbr: roughness/metalness overrides per park material. grade: contrast and saturation after tone mapping, vignette darkens the corners. weather: presets the menu cycles (after Clear), each overriding fog, sun, environment, exposure, and sky (fog = the fog colour instead of the sky), night (lamps glow, light pools under them, bloom); changes blend over a few seconds. lamps: park materials that glow at night. live (Weather → Live, src/client/liveweather.ts): where to ask Open-Meteo for the weather (lat, lon of the park), visibility under fogVisibility m or cloud over fogCloud % reads as fog (Karl, or Foggy night after dark), goldenMinutes after sunrise or before sunset is golden hour, refreshed every refreshMinutes. heightFog (Karl the Fog, weather heightFog 0..1): fog thick near the ground that thins upward (density per metre at base height in site metres, e-folding falloff metres), broken into banks by noise (noiseScale per metre) drifting with wind (m/s). bloom: the night glow (UnrealBloom strength, radius 0..1, threshold in linear light before tone mapping). nightSky (src/client/nightsky.ts): the night dome, zenith to horizon (keep horizon = the night fog colour so the city fades into it), glow = the warm city light band above the horizon, glowHeight its height (sine of elevation); stars (count, brightness; the glow washes out the low ones); moon dir (from the camera, z up), size (degrees), halo strength.

city._doc: The city around the park (world sf; src/client/city.ts). In the real look the sun's shadow map follows the skater: shadowReach = half the side of the shadowed square (m), shadowMap = its texels.
